items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: Bernie McGann, he sounds a bit like Sonny Rollins on alto, some people say he sounds a little bit of Ornette’s sound

ctx.x: He did mention that, I should have said that, I think that was his exception to what he was thinking. He was talking more about I believe like the pop music and jazz has been fashioned after music from somewhere else.

Yes, yes. I’m a lot older than Adrian, and I was fortunate enough to in the early 80s, I think it was ’83 is when there started to be a jazz course formed at Sydney Conservatorium. So I was there only five years into that program. And Nicki was in the same year also, the bass player I’m going to be playing with on Friday, and his name is Don Burrows. He only recently just passed away, an incredible clarinet, bari, he got me on bari. I owe him everything actually. I owe my career to Don Burrows. He, so this was…

at all either. It was sort of out of our reach financially and just was not available to us. But Bernie McGann, he sounds a bit like Sonny Rollins on alto, some people say he sounds a little bit of Ornette’s sound, that he was already playing that way before he even heard someone like Ornette Coleman. I do feel like Australia has created some quite unique and original sounding musicians who have a different way of, it’s influenced by American jazz but — yeah.
